title: ropeway:handbook-title-50
text: An aerial ropeway carries a cabin across ground you would rather not walk. A haul rope is strung from tower to tower, the cabin hangs from it on a grip, and it runs end to end and back again. The words Tower - the gantry you build. Every tower is the same structure; a tower with only one span attached is an end tower, and that is where the cabin stops. There is no separate station block. Span - one straight stretch of haul rope between two towers. Line - all the towers and spans chained end to end. Sheave - the grooved wheel in the pylon head that the rope runs through. Grip - the clamp on top of the cabin that holds it to the rope. Building a tower Place a pylon head where the rope should pass. It turns to face you as you place it, and the rest of the tower is measured from it: the rear gantry goes three blocks away from you, on the far side of the head. Look at a placed head - while the tower is unfinished the block info panel names the compass direction the rear gantry goes. You then build twenty-one more blocks by hand: - Two gantries, one at the pylon head and one three blocks behind it. - Each gantry is five ropeway braces wide across the top. The pylon head itself is the middle brace of the front gantry. - Under the outer brace of each gantry corner, three blocks of post: logs, debarked logs or planks, whichever wood you like. That leaves a clear three-wide, four-long, three-tall tunnel for the cabin to pass through. Right-click the pylon head at any time. If the tower is unfinished it tells you how many blocks are missing and lights up every cell that is wrong or empty - red where the wrong block sits, and the colour of the block it wants where nothing is. Look at the pylon head to read its state in the block info panel. Sneak and right-click the pylon head to open the tower guide: the build order in words, next to a turning 3D view of the two blocks the tower is made of and of the cabin itself. Next: Building a Line.
